header:
Meeting: POC weekly - edge routing & kernel experimentation
Date: 2026-08-12 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Acuity SRE), Ethan Ross (Acuity Platform), Lina Chen (Acuity Security), Tomás Rivera (Acuity Infra)
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on kernel experiment outcomes, transient egress failures, and routing fallback tuning. Discussed a kernel regression seen in canary, proposed rollback vs targeted patch, and agreed to run a focused bench and schedule a maintenance window for kernel upgrade. Security questions around audit logs and KMS surfaced; Redwood to supply SOC2 excerpts and key management notes.
topics: kernel regression analysis; egress timeout/fallbacks; prefix/KV caching behavior; routing policies and circuit breaker thresholds; security docs (SOC2/KMS); next steps and bench scheduling
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): All right folks good to see you, thanks for prioritizing this. Short agenda - kernel results, routing/fallbacks, security Qs, and next steps. Connor will start with the canary logs.
[01:05] Connor (SE): Hey everyone, I pulled the traces from the canary run last night. We saw increased syscall stalls around token 128 on long seqs, nvprof shows a tail of blocked warps, so it's likely a kernel change in the new cu-optimized path. There's also some K V cash thrash — K V cash was spelled out in one trace, I think the profiler mixed up the KV cache naming.
[03:20] Maya (Acuity SRE): Sorry to jump, when you say blocked warps that maps to GPU hang or just slower kernel? Because we had a few timeouts surfaced through our ingress LB.
[03:42] Connor (SE): It's slower, not a full hang, but it exacerbates queueing and that bubbled up as request timeouts at the V-P-C egress. So not all requests fail, more like tail latency spikes.
[04:15] Ethan (Acuity): We saw about 0.7% of requests hit the 2.5s timeout threshold during the canary window. Baseline was 0.1%. That difference is painful for user-facing flows.
[04:46] Sofia (AE): Important for scoping the rollback vs patch decision. Connor, is there a quick mitigation? Can we flip kernel flag or force the old codepath?
[05:10] Connor (SE): Yes we can toggle a runtime kernel flag to route to legacy kernels — it's a config change in the runtime, low risk. We can run a hotfix to flip traffic for the canary pool. That would be immediate but doesn't address root cause.
[05:38] Tomás (Acuity Infra): Hotfix sounds fine but we need change window and approval. Also worried about capacity impact if we re-route to legacy path — cost and latency tradeoff.
[06:05] Priya (Redwood CSM): Quick note: toggling will increase average p99 slightly but remove the tail spikes. We'll include cost delta in the follow-up note.
[06:28] Lina (Acuity Security): On security, we need to know if rolling back affects any cryptographic or KMS integrations. Also audit logs need to show model run provenance for compliance.
[06:46] Connor (SE): Rolling back is purely runtime kernel selection; no change to KMS or data plane. Audit logs will still capture the request/response IDs. We'll share the SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration note after this call.
[07:22] Maya (Acuity SRE): The egress failures looked like TCP resets and occasionally a malformed header at the load balancer. Could be MTU, could be our intermediate proxy. We opened a ticket on infra side to correlate.
[08:00] Ethan (Acuity): Also, when fallback occurs we saw more polyglot model selection — i.e. requests routed to smaller quantized models as fallback which changed response semantics. That caused a accuracy delta for intents.
[08:35] Sofia (AE): That's a key success criteria we discussed — no semantic regressions. We'll include a rollback to preserve semantics while we troubleshoot the kernel.
[09:00] Connor (SE): For troubleshooting, we'll need the nvprof and syslog dumps. I captured partials from the canary. I'll upload full traces to the shared folder. Expect a link in the notes.
[10:12] Maya (Acuity SRE): One more data point: our prefix cache hit-rate dropped during the spike window from 62% to 39%. Not sure if that's causal or symptomatic.
[10:40] Connor (SE): Could be both: slower kernels prolong token generation and evict prefixes more often; also our KV cache eviction policy might be too aggressive under memory pressure. We'll adjust eviction thresholds for the next run.
[12:00] Sofia (AE): Let's pivot to routing policies — Ethan tell us what you've observed in terms of circuit breaker trips and fallback ratios.
[12:22] Ethan (Acuity): Circuit breaker tripped 3x in the 2-hour canary window, each trip lasted ~2-3 minutes. Fallback to quantized models increased to 14% of traffic in those intervals. The current breakers are set at 4% error rate over a 60s sliding window. We might need a more granular per-route setting.
[13:05] Connor (SE): We can do per-route thresholds and also add a two-tier breaker: soft throttle then hard cutover. Soft throttle reduces inflight concurrency first which lowers tail pressure.
[13:40] Tomás (Acuity Infra): Sounds good— we need the exact config params so our infra team can mirror them. Also, can Redwood provide automated rollback if we detect semantic drift?
[14:05] Sofia (AE): We have A/B rollback flows — we can set a canary metric for semantic drift (intent match rate) and auto-fallback to pinned model version if drift exceeds threshold. We'll include a suggested threshold in the runbook.
[14:40] Lina (Acuity Security): On observability, what telemetry do you persist? We need longer retention for audit.
[15:00] Connor (SE): We persist request traces, model version, token counts, and latency histograms. By default retention is 30 days on hosted logs; for Private we can configure longer retention in our console and push to customer S3/GCS. We'll share specifics and a sample retention policy.
[15:34] Maya (Acuity SRE): Do you ship raw request payloads? For privacy we need to minimize PII retention.
[15:48] Connor (SE): We redact PII by default in telemetry and can support additional redaction rules. For Private deployments, data plane stays in the customer's VPC, we only get telemetry you opt-in to share.
[16:12] Ethan (Acuity): On the bench plan — we can run a 1k qps replay of last week's traffic with and without prefix cache to isolate eviction impact. We also want to try the legacy kernel path to measure p99 change. How long will you need to set that up?
[16:40] Connor (SE): We need the sample traces and we'll schedule bench runs. Setup is about half a day to configure the cluster and 2-3 hours to run and collect traces. We can run it in staging and provide aggregated metrics.
[17:12] Sofia (AE): Cost question — can you ballpark the delta if we keep the legacy path for the dedicated pool?
[17:25] Priya (CSM): Roughly a 10-18% increase in throughput cost per million tokens depending on batch sizes; I'll follow up with a more precise estimate after Connor shares actual qps numbers.
[18:00] Tomás (Acuity Infra): For the kernel upgrade window, we'll need a maintenance window and acceptance criteria. We're aiming for 2026-08-18 01:00-03:00 UTC if that works for Redwood.
[18:28] Sofia (AE): That should be doable. We'll plan the patch, test in canary, then roll to dedicated pool in the window if green.
[19:05] Lina (Acuity Security): Final security ask: can you provide the last SOC2 Type II report excerpts and confirm KMS/HSM integration patterns for private deployment?
[19:25] Connor (SE): Yes, I will share the SOC2 excerpt and a one-pager on KMS/HSM integration. For Private, customers can bring their own KMS.
[20:10] Maya (Acuity SRE): Quick ques — do you have automated alerts we can integrate with our pager duty?
[20:25] Priya (CSM): Yes, we can push alerts via webhook, and integrate with PD; we'll provide a sample alert subscription and recommended thresholds.
[21:00] Ethan (Acuity): Regarding the semantic drift check, can you include a set of unit prompts from our test-suite so we can quantify intent-match?
[21:20] Connor (SE): Absolutely, send the test-suite subset and we'll wire it into the canary health checks.
[22:10] Sofia (AE): Ok, let's recap quickly then call out owners.
[22:22] Sofia (AE): Recap — Connor will upload kernel traces and nvprof logs, and propose a targeted patch vs toggle. Maya will confirm the maintenance window. Ethan will provide traffic sample for bench. Sofia will send pricing delta and runbook. We'll bench prefix cache vs no-cache and legacy kernel vs optimized. Security docs SOC2 and KMS notes from Connor.
[23:05] Maya (Acuity SRE): One small note: when you upload traces can you anonymize hostnames? We can't share internal hostnames.
[23:24] Connor (SE): Yes, I'll scrub hostnames and any PII before upload.
[24:00] Tomás (Acuity Infra): Also please include the exact breaker settings and example config snippets.
[24:18] Connor (SE): Will do. We'll include suggested per-route breaker JSON and sample thresholds.
[25:00] Sofia (AE): Anything else?
[25:10] Lina (Acuity Security): None from security side.
[25:20] Ethan (Acuity): No.
[25:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll aim to have the runbook and pricing note by Monday.
[25:40] Sofia (AE): Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to logs and the bench schedule.
[26:00] [meeting winds down - casual chatter and goodbyes]
[51:55] End of recording.

Notes: The transcription has a few ASR artifacts: 'K V cash' for KV cache, 'V-P-C' for VPC. Speaker labels are best-effort mapping from the recording.
